data.narrative:
BRINC Drones, a Series C-stage defense and security drone manufacturer founded by Blake Resnick, has raised $157M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable set spanning 10 private firms and 2 public companies (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) within the Defense & Security sector.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement to the $157M raised proxy, yielding $267M. The peer-median approach examines three same-sector, same-stage comparables—Castelion ($13.0B), Stark Defence ($4.0B), and Neros ($2.5B)—generating a median valuation of $4.0B and a range of $2.5B to $13.0B. This peer set reflects substantial variation in scale, with the high end driven by Castelion's outlier valuation.

The triangulated valuation range spans $227M (low) to $4.6B (high), with a median of $2.1B. The wide dispersion reflects two competing signals: stage-progression modeling suggests BRINC remains in the sub-$300M range, while peer multiples imply valuations toward the top end of the defense tech market. Key uncertainties include revenue scale relative to comparables, customer concentration (defense procurement is contract-dependent), and technology differentiation within a crowded peer set. Investors should weight BRINC's specific commercial traction against the broad peer range before anchoring on any single point estimate.
